text: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make their own food. Plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make a sugar called glucose. Oxygen is released as a by-product. The green colour of leaves comes from a pigment called chlorophyll. Chlorophyll is found inside tiny structures in the leaf cells called chloroplasts. It absorbs energy from sunlight so the plant can make food. Plants take in water from the soil through their roots. The water travels up the stem to the leaves. Carbon dioxide enters the leaf from the air through tiny openings called stomata.

The glucose made during photosynthesis is used by the plant for energy and growth. Extra glucose is stored as starch in parts such as roots, seeds, and fruits. This is why potatoes and rice are rich in starch. Photosynthesis is important for all living things. It provides the oxygen that animals and humans breathe, and it is the starting point of most food chains, because animals eat plants or eat other animals that ate plants.
